# lemmon/id

> Random IDs optimized for visual transcription. Over audio, spell characters
> with code words such as Peter/Noro/Zuzana or Papa/November/Zulu; the library
> does not prevent bare letter names from being misheard. Zero runtime
> dependencies, one static class, six public methods.

## API

```php
use Lemmon\Id\Id;

Id::generate(int $length = 10, array $blocklist = self::DEFAULT_BLOCKLIST, ?int $maxConsecutive = null): string
Id::normalize(string $input): string
Id::isValid(string $id, ?int $length = null): bool
Id::chunk(string $id, int $chunkSize = 4, string $separator = '-'): string
Id::addCheck(string $id): string
Id::verifyCheck(string $id): bool
```

- `generate()` returns `$length - 1` random characters and one deterministic
  check character. It retries at most 100 times against the complete candidate
  and throws below length 2, below `maxConsecutive` 1, or when the blocklist
  or `maxConsecutive` cannot be satisfied. `maxConsecutive` is off by default;
  set it to reject a candidate (including its check character) where the same
  character repeats more than that many times in a row. Use with caution —
  low values sharply shrink the valid candidate pool.
- `normalize()` removes Unicode whitespace, Unicode dashes, the minus sign,
  invisible format characters (e.g. zero-width space), and `.`, `_`, `-`; applies
  selected case-aware repairs (`g`,`q`→`9`; `v`→`y`; `G`→`c`; `V`→`y`;
  `1`→`7`; `2`→`z`); and lowercases. On invalid UTF-8, separator removal is
  skipped but ASCII corrections and lowercasing still run. It does not
  validate length or checksum.
- `isValid()` checks alphabet membership and optional exact length, not the
  checksum.
- `chunk()` groups Unicode grapheme clusters for display and throws below
  chunk size 1. The default separator round-trips through `normalize()`.
- `addCheck()` appends a check character to a non-empty, unchecked body made
  only from alphabet characters.
- `verifyCheck()` validates alphabet membership and the trailing check
  character. It expects normalized input and does not enforce an expected
  length.

For a fixed ten-character format, validate user input with both checks:

```php
$id = Id::normalize($typed);
$valid = Id::isValid($id, 10) && Id::verifyCheck($id);
```

## Alphabet and check

Alphabet: `3479cdefhjkmnprtwxyz`.

It was selected to reduce common glyph confusion in lowercase and uppercase;
this is not a typeface-independent guarantee. Confusion groups may be removed
entirely or represented by one survivor. Only excluded characters with a
case-specific, unambiguous target are repaired.

The trailing character is a Luhn mod 20 checksum. It detects every
single-character substitution and every adjacent transposition except
`3` ↔ `z`. It never detects swaps of characters one position apart
(`cdf` → `fdc`) and misses about 4% of doubled-pair substitutions
(`cc` → `dd`). A uniformly random string drawn from the alphabet passes with
1-in-20 probability. It is not a security feature.

## Blocklist and limits

`a` is excluded to make several unwanted words structurally impossible. The
default blocklist contains a short, selected set of unwanted English terms and
initialisms still expressible by the alphabet. It is intentionally not
exhaustive or multilingual. Callers can extend, replace, or disable it; the
authoritative list is `Id::DEFAULT_BLOCKLIST`.

The library does not handle persistence or collisions. Enforce a unique
database constraint and retry on conflict. Do not use these IDs as secrets,
tokens, or capability URLs.
